1936年6月11日被判处监禁14个月并罚款2,800里拉。

On October 5, 1936, Pinto was deported
from Shanghai by the Judge of the Royal Italian
Consular Court and departed on the S.S. "Conte
Rosso" presumably to serve the sentence of two
years' imprisonment imposed in June that year
in a penitentiary on Rhodes Island off the South
West coast of Asia Minor.

Pinto has not again come to the notice

THE CHINA PRESS, TUESDAY, OCTOBER 6, 1936
16-920
4777
6 10 36

Pinto Leaves
To Serve Jail
Term In Italy

Will Finish Time Given
For Robbing His Own
Bank Here

Vincent Pinto, erstwhile Shanghai banker, money-lender and hotel owner, was among the persons departing for Italy on the liner Conte Rosso which sailed from this city about 6.30 p.m. yesterday. Pinto is going home to complete serving a two-year prison sentence which was given him by the Italian Consular Court in June of this year after he had been convicted of robbing his own bank in an effort to defraud the International Assurance Company, Ltd.

Since his conviction, Pinto has been confined in the Ward Road Jail. On three occasions, however, he has been brought outside the jail walls to visit the consular court where he was the defendant in a series of lawsuits and another criminal charge, the latter involving usury. He lost the usury case and was fined. He was also fined lira 7,500 in connection with the fraud case and his total fines now aggregate lira 10,000.

All cases against Pinto closed, the consular court officials decided to send him back to Italy to complete the remainder of his sentence. Just what prison he will be sent to upon his return to Italy was not stated by the authorities. The man was handed over to the captain of the Conte Rosso yesterday afternoon and it is understood will be kept in confinement during the trip home. Only a few very close friends were at the boat to say good-bye to him.

Pinto, who opened a bank on Nanking Road near the corner of Kiangse Road about two years ago, attained headlines in October of last year when he called in the police to investigate a burglary. Someone had broken into his safe, he said, and had stolen cash and some jewelry to the total value of $90,000. The safe door had been chiseled open while the lock on the bank entrance had been broken.

Pinto's activities in the past had attracted police attention and there was naturally some suspicion that the burglary might have been an inside job. The man had once served a sentence in the Amoy Road Jail for purchasing stolen property.

Investigation of the case was placed in the charge of Detective Sub-Inspector A. G. Tilton. The latter, after several months, obtained sufficient evidence to convict Pinto of fraud and the man was accordingly brought into court. THE SHANGHAI TIMES, FRIDAY, JUNE 19, 1936

Pinto Is Given Ten Months'
Term On Usury Count

Italian Banker Also Fined 5,000 Liras; To Serve In
All Two Years, Having Already Received 14
Months' Sentence For Attempted Fraud

V. Pinto, Italian manager and director of the bank (an exchange and loan institution) bearing his name, was sentenced to a further 10 months' imprisonment and a fine of 5,000 liras in the Italian Consular Court yesterday, upon being found guilty of usury.

Pinto has now to serve a sentence of two years' imprisonment and has to pay a total fine of 7,800 liras (amounting to about $2,300) as on June 11, he was sentenced in the same court to 14 months' imprisonment and was fined 2,800 liras, upon being found guilty by Judge R. Rapex and two assessors of attempting to defraud an insurance company.

The prosecution against Pinto arose out of his claim that over the week-end of September 14 to 16, last, the premises of the Pinto Bank, on the first floor of 166 Nanking Road, were broken into and money and jewellery to the amount of $63,000 stolen. Pinto claimed the sum from the International Assurance Compnay, Limited, who after investigating the circumstances surrounding the burglary, refused to pay him anything. He filed an action against them in the British Supreme Court. In the meantime the circumstances surrounding the burglary were investigated by the Italian Consular authorities and the Shanghai Municipal Police.

At the end of May, summonses were served on Pinto and Mrs. Anna Caccioppoli, Italian proprietor of the Victor Hotel and Italian Restaurant at 216 Range Road, to appear before the Italian Consular Court on June 9, to answer to a charge of attempting to defraud an insurance company. Investigations in the meantime were continued and as a result of further evidence being brought to light Pinto was arrested on Saturday evening, June 6, and held in custody pending his trial. The trial opened on Tuesday, June 9, and following a great deal of sensational evidence Pinto was convicted and sentenced. Mrs. Anna Caccioppoli was found guilty of complicity in the case and was sentenced to six months' imprisonment and fined 1,200 liras. Her fine was however, suspended for five years.

Took Only One Per Cent

At his trial yesterday on the charge of usury, Pinto maintained that he had only charged the legal rate of interest, one per cent. per month. Upon being pressed by Judge Rapex he admitted that he sometimes charged two per cent., but these included various commissions, insurance and brokerage. Upon being confronted with his own books in which it was entered that $126 in interest was received for a loan of $1,818, he could not very well explain it, finally stating that the interest referred to another account.

At the start of the hearing yesterday Mr. Fausto Ferrera, an Italian accountant gave expert evidence. He stated that he had examined the books of the Pinto Bank. He mentioned that they had not been kept in a proper manner and were very complicated. With reference to one of the complainants in the usury case he stated that he found that Mr. Garjuillo, proprietor of the Marcel Beauty Parlour, had paid only one per cent. Italian interest per month. On another occasion however, three per cent. was charged. Pinto interposed at this stage to say that Mr. Garjuillo could not return the loan when due and himself offered to pay three per cent. for the period of the extension.

Cell-mate Called

V. V. Tatisheff, 34-year-old Russian, who is at present serving a two months' term of imprisonment for misappropriation, and who was a cell-mate of Pinto's at the Central Police Station, was again called to testify yesterday. Tatisheff stated that Pinto had bragged to him that "it was easy for him to get money from idiots." Tatisheff also stated that Pinto had told him that he received 12 per cent. interest on money loaned (that was legal), but on top of that he (Pinto) "resorted to various tricks, such as charging commissions, insurance and brokerage." On diamonds Pinto was alleged to have said that he charged 20 per cent. interest, as diamonds depreciated in value, and as much as 30 per cent. on real estate.

Pinto denied that he ever had talked to Tatisheff and alleged that all this was just a police "frame-up."

Mrs. Caccioppoli was also called to stand and asked to relate how she had collected money from Mr. Garjuillo. She stated that she had done so as a favour to both Pinto and Mr. Garjuillo. She said that Mr. Garjuillo used to repay the loan in installments of $20, $15 and $10 several times a week. She denied ever having collected any interest, saying that she only received the principal.

Lawyers Speak Long

At the conclusion of the evidence long addresses were made by the two counsel for the defence, Messrs. G. Constantini and R. D'Auxion de Ruffe. Mr. Constantini made an impassioned appeal on behalf of his client in Italian. He contended that Pinto had not charged a high rate of interest and if he did, he did not do so from people in dire need, but from people who borrowed money for luxuries.

Mr. D'Auxion de Ruffe admitted that the rate of interest charged by Pinto was not strictly legal and that Pinto sometimes did charge high interest, but then the lawyer asked the court to take into consideration what a risk Pinto was taking and that if he did collect high interest from one person, he lost both the interest and the money loaned in another case. In asking the court to dismiss the case, Mr. de Ruffe termed it as "much ado about nothing."

Judge Rapex and the two assessors, Comm. de Lucca and Cav. L. Bedoni, adjourned for about half-an-hour after which Judge Rapex read out the judgment and passed the sentence in the name of the "King of Italy and Emperor of Ethiopia."

平托因高利贷罪
被判十个月徒刑

这位意大利银行家还被罚款5,000里拉；总计需服刑两年，此前已因企图欺诈罪获刑14个月

V. 平托，以其名字命名的银行（一家汇兑与贷款机构）的意大利经理兼董事，昨日在意大利领事法庭因被裁定犯有高利贷罪，被追加判处10个月监禁并罚款5,000里拉。

平托现在需服刑两年，并需支付总计7,800里拉（约合2,300美元）的罚款，因为他在6月11日已在同一法庭被R. 拉佩克斯（R. Rapex）法官及两名陪审推事裁定犯有企图欺诈保险公司罪，判处14个月监禁并罚款2,800里拉。

对平托的起诉源于他声称在去年9月14日至16日的周末，位于南京路166号一楼的平托银行 premises 遭人闯入，价值63,000美元的现金和珠宝被盗。平托向国际保险公司有限公司索赔这笔款项，该公司在调查盗窃案周围情况后拒绝支付任何赔偿。他随后在英国最高法院对该公司提起诉讼。与此同时，意大利领事当局和上海公共租界工部局警务处对盗窃案周围的情况进行了调查。

5月底，传票送达平托以及兰格路216号维克多酒店和意大利餐厅的意大利业主安娜·卡乔波利夫人（Mrs. Anna Caccioppoli），要求他们于6月9日出庭意大利领事法庭，就企图欺诈保险公司的指控进行答辩。期间的调查仍在继续，随着更多证据浮出水面，平托于6月6日星期六晚间被捕，并在候审期间被羁押。审判于6月9日星期二开庭，在经过大量耸人听闻的举证后，平托被定罪并判刑。安娜·卡乔波利夫人被裁定在该案中犯有共谋罪，判处六个月监禁并罚款1,200里拉。不过，她的罚款缓刑五年执行。

仅收取百分之一利息

在昨日的高利贷罪庭审中，平托坚称他只收取法定利率，即每月百分之一。在拉佩克斯法官的追问下，他承认有时收取百分之二的利息，但称其中包含了各种佣金、保险费和经纪费。当面对他自己的账簿，其中记载一笔1,818美元的贷款收取了126美元利息时，他无法很好地解释，最后声称该利息指的是另一笔账户。

在昨日听证会开始时，意大利会计师福斯托·费雷拉（Fausto Ferrera）先生提供了专家证词。他表示已检查了平托银行的账簿。他提到这些账簿保管不当，且非常复杂。关于高利贷案中的一名投诉人，他指出发现马塞尔美容厅（Marcel Beauty Parlour）业主加尔朱伊洛（Garjuillo）先生每月仅支付了百分之一的意大利利息。然而在另一次，收取的利息为百分之三。平托在此阶段插话说，加尔朱伊洛先生到期无法偿还贷款，是他自己提出在延期期间支付百分之三的利息。

传唤狱友

34岁的俄罗斯人V. V. 塔蒂谢夫（V. V. Tatisheff）目前正因挪用公款罪服刑两个月，他曾在中央巡捕房与平托同囚一室，昨日再次被传唤作证。塔蒂谢夫称，平托曾向他吹嘘“从傻瓜那里弄钱很容易”。塔蒂谢夫还称，平托告诉他，借出的资金收取12%的利息（这是合法的），但除此之外，他（平托）“使用各种伎俩，如收取佣金、保险费和经纪费”。据称平托在钻石方面表示收取20%的利息，理由是钻石会贬值，而在房地产方面则高达30%。

平托否认曾与塔蒂谢夫交谈，并指控这一切都是警方的“栽赃陷害”。

卡乔波利夫人也被传唤出庭，并被要求讲述她如何从加尔朱伊洛先生那里收取款项。她表示这样做是出于对平托和加尔朱伊洛先生双方的好意。她说加尔朱伊洛先生通常每周分几次偿还贷款，金额分别为20美元、15美元和10美元。她否认曾收取任何利息，称她只收回本金。

律师长篇陈词

在举证结束后，两位辩护律师G. 康斯坦蒂尼（G. Constantini）先生和R. 多克西翁·德·鲁菲（R. D'Auxion de Ruffe）先生发表了长篇演说。康斯坦蒂尼先生用意大利语为其当事人作了充满激情的恳求。他辩称，平托并未收取高息，即使收了，也不是向急需帮助的人收取，而是向那些借钱用于奢侈消费的人收取。

德·鲁菲先生承认平托收取的利率并不完全合法，且平托有时确实收取高息，但随后该律师请求法庭考虑平托所承担的风险，并指出如果他从一个人那里收取了高息，在另一个案件中他却既损失了利息也损失了本金。在请求法庭驳回此案时，德·鲁菲先生称其为“无事生非”。

拉佩克斯法官及两名陪审推事卢卡专员（Comm. de Lucca）和L. 贝多尼骑士（Cav. L. Bedoni）休庭约半小时，随后拉佩克斯法官宣读了判决书，并以“意大利国王暨埃塞俄比亚皇帝”的名义宣判。

VERDICT GIVEN IN
PINTO CASE

Two Defendants Both Fined
and Sent to Prison

APPEAL TO BE HEARD IN
RHODES

No sooner had judgment on P
Pinto, manager and director of the
Pinto Bank, been pronounced in the
Italian Consular Court yesterday
than the hearing of another case
commenced, Pinto being charged on
this count with exacting illegally
high rates of interest on loans to
two other parties. Judgment on the
first case, brought against Pinto and
Mrs. A. Cacciopoli for defrauding
the International Assurance Com-
pany, Ltd., was pronounced by Cav.
R. Rapex, Italian Consular Judge.
as follows: Pinto to serve 14 months'
imprisonment, and to pay a fine of
2,000 lire; Mrs. Cacciopoli to serve
six months' imprisonment, and to
pay a fine of 200 lire. The latter
sentence was suspended for five
years.

The case brought for defrauding
the insurance company commenced
on Tuesday, when a number of wit-
nesses gave evidence, and was
brought to a crux yesterday morning
when a Russian by the name of
Count T. T. Tatisheff, who had been
confined in the same cell as Pinto
at the Central Police Station, related
intimate conversations which, he
said, had taken place between him
and Pinto. In the course of these
conversations, Tatisheff declared,
Pinto had made plans for Tatisheff
to escape from Shanghai, and had men-
tioned the name of a third party to
whom Tatisheff could apply for a
false passport if Pinto were still
detained in prison.

It is understood that Pinto's coun-
sel has already filed an appeal
against this decision, and that this
will be heard before a court of
appeal in the Island of Rhodes.
Counsel for the defence in the first
action were M. d'Auxion de Ruffe
and Dr. G. Costantini.

High Rates of Interest

The second case concerns the
dealings of Pinto with two other
Italians named Carisio and Gargullo.
Carisio said that he had at one time
asked Pinto for $500. Pinto had
given him $480, and he had paid
back the sum of $600 on the loan.
Another time, he borrowed $350,
and paid back $424, and on August
1 last he borrowed $500, and paid
back the sum of $586.

By defendant's request, the evi-
dence of Mr. G. V. Bykovsky was
then taken, and the next witness,
Mr. Bruno Rubini, said that he had
applied to Pinto for the sum of $150,
and Pinto had given him about $130
in compliance with his request, on
six promissory notes. With this sum,
Rubini paid an employee of Pinto's,
Russo, and the latter then went to
Pinto's Bank and explained that
Rubini had handed over the money
to him. Pinto denied having been
paid a call by Russo with regard to
this loan.

Mr. Gargullo said that he had
received from Pinto the sum of £30
and $100, to send to his brother in
Italy, and he paid Pinto five per
cent. per month on this loan. In
June last, he borrowed $500 from
Pinto, and paid on this 15 per cent.
interest per month. He had also
borrowed a further sum at a high
rate of interest.

The evidence of V. Lasinska,
Pinto's secretary, was then taken and
the case was adjourned until next
Thursday.

平托案宣判

并监禁

上诉将在罗得岛审理

意大利领事法庭昨日刚对平托银行经理兼董事 P. 平托（P. Pinto）一案作出判决，另一起案件的审讯随即开始。在此案中，平托被指控向另外两方非法收取高额贷款利息。针对平托和 A. 卡乔波利夫人（Mrs. A. Cacciopoli）欺诈国际保险公司（International Assurance Company, Ltd.）的第一起案件，由意大利领事法官 R. 拉佩克斯骑士（Cav. R. Rapex）宣判如下：平托判处监禁14个月，并处罚金2000里拉；卡乔波利夫人判处监禁6个月，并处罚金200里拉。后者的刑罚缓刑五年。

欺诈保险公司一案于周二开庭，多名证人出庭作证，并于昨日上午达到关键阶段。当时，一名名为 T. T. 塔蒂谢夫伯爵（Count T. T. Tatisheff）的俄国人出庭作证，他此前曾因与平托关押在中央捕房同一间牢房而相识，讲述了据称发生在他与平托之间的私密谈话。塔蒂谢夫声称，在这些谈话中，平托制定了帮助塔蒂谢夫逃离上海的计划，并提到如果平托仍被拘押在狱中，塔蒂谢夫可以向某第三方申请假护照，平托还提到了该第三方的名字。

据悉，平托的辩护律师已对此判决提出上诉，该上诉将由罗得岛（Rhodes）的上诉法庭审理。第一起诉讼中的辩护律师为 M. d'Auxion de Ruffe 和 G. Costantini 博士。

高利率

第二起案件涉及平托与另外两名意大利人 Carisio 和 Gargullo 的交易。Carisio 称，他曾一度向平托借款500美元。平托给了他480美元，而他偿还了600美元。另一次，他借款350美元，偿还了424美元；去年8月1日，他借款500美元，偿还了586美元。

应被告请求，法庭随后听取了 G. V. Bykovsky 先生的证词。下一位证人 Bruno Rubini 先生表示，他曾向平托申请借款150美元，平托应其要求，凭六张本票给了他约130美元。Rubini 用这笔钱支付给平托的一名雇员 Russo，后者随后前往平托银行，解释说 Rubini 已将钱交给他。平托否认 Russo 曾就这笔贷款事宜拜访过他。

Gargullo 先生称，他从平托处收到30英镑和100美元，用于汇给其在意大利的兄弟，他为此笔贷款每月向平托支付5%的利息。去年6月，他向平托借款500美元，为此每月支付15%的利息。他还以高利率借入了另一笔款项。

随后听取了平托秘书 V. Lasinska 的证词，案件休庭至下周四。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, THURSDAY, JUNE 11, 1936 14924
RUSSIAN COUNT IN SAME CELL WITH PINTO

Sensational Evidence Given Yesterday at Conclusion of Case Brought for Alleged Fraud

A SENSATIONAL climax brought to a conclusion yesterday the case against V. Pinto, manager and director of the Pinto Bank, and Mrs. A. Cacciopoli, who are being charged with defrauding the International Assurance Co., Ltd., in the Italian Consular Court before Cav. R. Rapex, Italian Consular Judge. Counsel for the defence were M. d'Auxion de Ruffe and Dr. G. Costantini. A witness brought by the police, Count T. T. Tatisheff, who was put in the same cell as Pinto, after having been charged with the misappropriation of a typewriter, related the conversations alleged to have taken place between the accused and himself, even up to conversation which took place after the commencement of the trial, when Pinto gave his impressions of the legal proceedings.

The case follows a robbery at the bank during the week-end of September 14-16, 1935, the sum involved being $63,000. An action against the International Assurance Co., who refused to pay the claim made against them after the robbery, was instituted some time ago in H.M. Supreme Court, but was withdrawn.

In his evidence, Count Tatisheff said that he met Pinto for the first time on Saturday in a cell in the Central Police Station, when he conversed with him in four languages, French, Italian, Spanish and English. He asked him why he was in gaol and Pinto told him the reason.

The Judge: Did Pinto say something confidentially to you?—He was very nervous, and started to talk about his private affairs.

Witness stated that he was warned by the police that if he kept what Pinto told him to himself, he would be considered as an accomplice of Pinto's. Pinto told him that at the age of 13½ he left his home, and started out in life. After a time, he went over to France.

The Judge: Did he say anything about white slaves?—Yes.

Pinto stopped his business in France, witness continued, because the French police interfered, and he then came to Shanghai. Here he continued his activities in various branches, mostly illegal. Pinto told him that he was a banker, and had started an establishment in Nanking Road, which transacted every kind of banking business. He mentioned the fact that he had several friends in Shanghai and gave the names of some of them. Other intimate details were disclosed, and Pinto confided to him that he was almost certain to get free.

"A Good Friend"

He saw Pinto again on Tuesday morning, when he said that he was practically certain to be acquitted because there were no charges against him. On Wednesday morning, Pinto told him that if the case went wrong he had a good friend who would pay his accounts, mentioning the name of Mr. Russo. When he saw him on Tuesday morning, he said that things were going very well in court. The first case, which was the claim of the insurance company, was going to be finished on Wednesday afternoon, and there was another case with regard to loans, etc.

Pinto told him that he was financially interested in several establishments, including a cabaret and even a gambling house. To open the latter, he had to bribe the police with $10,000, but they took the money, and then closed the house five or six days later. The last business he ran was an import and export branch. Pinto told him that he had cultivated nose bleeding in order to be taken over to the Ward Road gaol which was more comfortable. He saw Pinto on Wednesday morning for the last time, when he asked him where he had to report if Pinto were still detained. Pinto told him to go to Russo, who would provide him with a false passport, with which to escape from Shanghai.

M. de Ruffe, (cross-examining): What is your real name?—Count Tatisheff.

Did you not introduce yourself to the Shanghai public as a representative of the Hearst Newspaper Syndicate?—No.

Counsel stated that this story had been carried by the "Shanghai Zaria."

Did you have any previous criminal records in other countries?—No.

You say that these conversations with Pinto in gaol took place in French and other languages?—Yes. Pinto understood French very well.

No Knowledge of French

M. de Ruffe: When Pinto comes to my office, he always has to have an interpreter. He does not understand French. It is quite unbelievable that he can converse in that language.

M. de Ruffe further brought out that an amicable settlement had been reached between the witness and the people who put him in gaol, this having been concluded the previous day.

Summing up, M. de Ruffe said that what insurance companies hated to do was to pay up when the time came. He had come to the conclusion that unless there had been any miscounting in the books of the Pinto Bank, there had been no defrauding of the insurance company. The state of the books had nothing to do with the robbery itself. The first time that it had been suggested that Pinto was responsible for the robbing of the bank was in the evidence of the last witness. The police had done their best to find out who was responsible for the robbery, but they had not found that the Pinto Bank or any of its employees were responsible. It was probably arranged, he declared, by the same gang as had performed the same kind of trick before, once to a jewellery firm in the same block as the Pinto Bank, which was burgled about two years ago, and once again when the premises of Sennet Freres was burgled, about a year ago. They must consider the fact that Pinto's premises were burgled as being apart from the case.

It was absurd to say that a person with average intelligence would have talked about having a robbery of his premises two years before it was supposed to take place, and to have prepared his books accordingly. The alleged mistakes in the books had probably been made in the best of faith. No bank would carry on for months, and even years, and fix a definite date on which a burglary was to take place.

Entries Under Assumed Names

There was one point which had probably surprised and possibly shocked the court, and this was the entries in the account books under assumed names. Strictly speaking, such a procedure was not etiquette, but they must consider the country in which they were living, and the circumstances existing in Shanghai were such that it was not surprising that Pinto had accounts under assumed names. All people in business knew it as a fact that assumed names were used for accounts. A previous witness, from the firm of Messrs. Lowe, Bingham and Matthews, had denied knowledge of the practice, but he would refer the court to an article in a local newspaper dealing with the subject.

Pinto's business was lending money. There was nothing dishonourable in that but people did not like their names mentioned in connection with it. Those who borrowed money from Pinto asked him not to mention their names in the books. They had also heard that a considerable amount of money, over $40,000 in bank notes, had been seen in the safes. If Pinto wanted the good position of the bank proved in the most conclusive manner, he had only to camouflage the real amount by wrapping it up in paper and making it look much more than it really was. It had also been stated that Pinto's business was not such that there would have been such a considerable amount of money in the safes at the time of the robbery.

Moneylenders' Methods

"But these moneylenders keep their money in cash," declared M. de Ruffe, "they do not give cheques because they deduct from the money given the interest to be paid, which is often more than the law permits. Moneylenders very rarely advance money to their customers by cheque."

After pointing out four alleged mistakes in the report of the police, M. de Ruffe said that it had never been proved that the business purchased by Mrs. Cacciopoli was a faked concern. The court could not condemn Pinto because the element of doubt was too great. There may have been mistakes made, but the premeditated intention to defraud the insurance company had not been proved. He would not speak of the evidence of the last witness. It was, however, most surprising to hear that somebody had paid up for this witness, and he was now free.

In a long summing up given in Italian, Dr. Costantini brought the proceedings to a close early in the afternoon, and, after a recess, it was announced that judgment would be delivered this morning at 8.30.

In the report of Tuesday's proceedings, mention was made of a firm of chartered accountants who had signed the balance sheet of the Pinto Bank. This was not a firm of chartered accountants but of public accountants.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE

《字林西报》，1936年6月11日，星期四 14924
俄国伯爵与平托同囚一室

昨日在涉嫌欺诈案结案时提供惊人证词

昨日，针对平托银行经理兼董事 V. 平托（V. Pinto）和 A. 卡乔波利夫人（Mrs. A. Cacciopoli）的案件在意大利领事法庭结案，二人被控欺诈国际保险公司（International Assurance Co., Ltd.）。庭审由意大利领事法官 R. 拉佩克斯骑士（Cav. R. Rapex）主持。辩护律师为 M. d'Auxion de Ruffe 和 G. Costantini 博士。警方传唤的一名证人 T. T. 塔蒂谢夫伯爵（Count T. T. Tatisheff）曾因挪用打字机被控，并与平托关押在同一间牢房。他讲述了据称发生在被告与他之间的对话，甚至包括审判开始后进行的谈话，当时平托谈了他对法律诉讼的看法。

此案源于1935年9月14日至16日周末期间银行发生的一起抢劫案，涉案金额为63,000美元。此前曾向英国最高法院提起诉讼，控告拒绝赔付抢劫后索赔的国际保险公司，但该诉讼已被撤回。

塔蒂谢夫伯爵在证词中表示，他于周六在中央捕房的一间牢房里首次见到平托，当时他用四种语言——法语、意大利语、西班牙语和英语——与平托交谈。他问平托为何入狱，平托告诉了他原因。

法官：平托是否私下对你说了什么？——他非常紧张，开始谈论他的私事。

证人表示，警方警告他，如果他对平托告诉他的话保密，他将被视为平托的同谋。平托告诉他，他在13岁半时离家，开始独立生活。过了一段时间，他去了法国。

法官：他有没有提到关于白奴贸易的事？——有。

证人继续说，平托在法国的生意因为法国警方的干涉而停止，随后他来到上海。在这里，他继续从事各种行业的活动，大多是非法的。平托告诉他，他是一名银行家，并在南京路开设了一家机构，经营各类银行业务。他提到他在上海有几个朋友，并说出了其中一些人的名字。其他私密细节也被披露，平托向他吐露，他几乎肯定能获得自由。

“一位好朋友”

他在周二上午再次见到平托，当时平托说他几乎肯定会被无罪释放，因为对他没有指控。周三上午，平托告诉他，如果案子出问题，他有一位好朋友会替他还账，并提到了 Russo 先生的名字。当他在周二上午见到平托时，平托说法庭上的情况进展顺利。第一起案件，即保险公司的索赔案，将于周三下午结案，还有另一起关于贷款等的案件。

平托告诉他，他在几家机构中有经济利益，包括一家歌舞厅，甚至一家赌场。为了开设后者，他不得不向警方行贿10,000美元，但警方收了钱后，却在五六天后关闭了该场所。他经营的最后一项业务是进出口部门。平托告诉他，他故意诱发流鼻血，以便被转送到条件更舒适的华德路监狱。他在周三上午最后一次见到平托，当时他问平托，如果平托仍被拘押，他该去哪里报到。平托让他去找 Russo，Russo 会为他提供一本假护照，以便逃离上海。

M. de Ruffe（交叉询问）：你的真名是什么？——塔蒂谢夫伯爵。

你难道不是以赫斯特报业辛迪加（Hearst Newspaper Syndicate）代表的身份向上海公众自我介绍的吗？——不是。

辩护律师指出，这个故事曾被《上海柴拉报》（Shanghai Zaria）刊登。

你在其他国家有犯罪前科吗？——没有。

你说这些与平托在狱中的谈话是用法语和其他语言进行的？——是的。平托非常懂法语。

不懂法语

M. de Ruffe：当平托来到我的办公室时，他总是需要一名翻译。他不懂法语。他能用法语交谈是完全不可信的。

M. de Ruffe 还指出，证人与将他送进监狱的人之间已达成友好和解，该和解于前一天达成。

在总结陈词中，M. de Ruffe 表示，保险公司最不愿意做的事就是在到期时付款。他得出的结论是，除非平托银行的账目有任何计算错误，否则不存在欺诈保险公司的行为。账目的状况与抢劫案本身无关。首次暗示平托对银行抢劫案负责的是最后一位证人的证词。警方已尽力查明谁对抢劫案负责，但他们并未发现平托银行或其任何员工对此负责。他宣称，这很可能是由同一个团伙策划的，该团伙以前也玩过同样的伎俩，一次是针对与平托银行在同一街区的一家珠宝公司，该公司大约在两年前被盗；另一次是针对 Sennet Freres 的 premises，大约在一年前被盗。他们必须考虑到，平托的营业场所被盗这一事实应与本案分开看待。

说一个具有普通智力的人会在预计发生抢劫的两年前就谈论此事，并相应地准备账目，这是荒谬的。所谓的账目错误可能是出于善意造成的。没有哪家银行会连续数月甚至数年运营，并确定一个发生入室盗窃的具体日期。

使用化名记账

有一点可能令法庭感到惊讶，甚至震惊，那就是账簿中使用化名进行的记录。严格来说，这种程序不符合规范，但他们必须考虑他们所生活的国家，上海的情况使得平托使用化名开立账户并不令人惊讶。所有商界人士都知道，使用化名记账是一个事实。前一位来自 Lowe, Bingham and Matthews 公司的证人否认知晓这种做法，但他提请法庭注意当地报纸上关于此主题的一篇文章。

平托的业务是放贷。这并无不光彩之处，但人们不喜欢自己的名字与此相关联。向平托借钱的人要求他不要在账簿中提到他们的名字。他们还听说，有人看到保险箱里有大量现金，超过40,000美元的钞票。如果平托想以最确凿的方式证明银行的良好状况，他只需用纸包裹真实金额，使其看起来比实际多得多。此外，还有人声称，平托的业务性质决定了在抢劫发生时，保险箱里不会有如此大量的现金。

放债人的手段

“但是这些放债人将钱以现金形式保存，” M. de Ruffe 宣称，“他们不开支票，因为他们从给出的金额中扣除要支付的利息，这往往超过法律允许的范围。放债人很少通过支票向客户预付款项。”

在指出警方报告中的四处所谓错误后，M. de Ruffe 表示，从未证明卡乔波利夫人购买的企业是虚假的。法庭不能定罪平托，因为疑点太大。可能会有错误发生，但蓄意欺诈保险公司的意图未被证实。他不会谈论最后一位证人的证词。然而，听到有人为这位证人付了款，且他现在已获自由，这最令人惊讶。

Costantini 博士用意大利语作了长篇总结陈词，于下午早些时候结束了诉讼程序。休庭后，宣布将于今晨8:30宣判。

在周二诉讼程序的报告中，提到了一家签署平托银行资产负债表的特许会计师行。这并非一家特许会计师行，而是一家公共会计师行。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, MONDAY, JUNE 8, 1936

Pinto Placed
Under Arrest
After Inquiry

Head Of Bank Detained
At Ward Road Gaol
On Court Warrant

TO FACE TRIAL WITH
WOMAN TO-MORROW

Four Lawyers Are Retained
For Defence; Scene At
The Consulate

Mr. V. Pinto, Italian manager and director of the Pinto Bank, an exchange and loan institution, who, at the end of last month was served with a summons to appear before the Italian Consular Court tomorrow to answer charges of an attempt to defraud an insurance company, as reported exclusively in "The Shanghai Times" on May 25, was placed under arrest on Saturday night and yesterday was confined in the Ward Road Gaol on a consular warrant pending his trial.

Mr. Pinto was arrested, it is understood, as a result of certain details being brought to light during the investigations into the previous charge conducted by the consular authorities and detectives of Central Police Station.

At the end of May, both Pinto and Mrs. A Caccioppoli, who reside in and, it is understood, operate the Victor Hotel and Italian Restaurant at 216 Range Road, were served with summonses to appear before the Italian Consular Court on the morning of June 9 (to-morrow) to answer charges of an attempt to defraud an insurance company. The charge arises out of the $63,000 cash and jewel robbery staged at the Pinto Bank with offices on the first floor of 166 Nanking Road, over the week-end of October 14 and 16, last, which was subject of a thorough police investigation. It is understood that the insurance company concerned refused to pay over the insurance money. Action was instituted in the British Supreme Court against the insurance company, but was later withdrawn.

It was understood at the time that summonses were served against Mr. Pinto and Mrs. Caccioppoli that there was strong evidence against them, but later further facts were brought to light which caused a warrant to be issued for the arrest of Mr. Pinto.

Armed with a consular warrant, it is reported detectives of Central Police Station proceeded to the Viktor Hotel on Range Road on Saturday evening and there awaited the return home of Mr. Pinto. They placed him under arrest and brought him back to Central Police Station, where he spent the night.

Before Judge

In the morning, Pinto was taken to the Italian Consular Court and brought before Cav. Uff. R. Rapex, Consular Judge. It is understood that during the short period that Pinto was at the Italian Court, there were several scenes, with Pinto not feeling very well. Finally an order was issued by the Italian authorities to confine Pinto in the Ward Road Gaol pending his appearance before the court tomorrow morning together with Mrs. Cacciopollì.

In the same manner as when the summonses were served upon the two Italians, both the Italian authorities and the police maintained complete silence as to the exact nature of the allegations against Pinto and Mr. Cacciopollì. Judge Rapex confirmed the fact that Pinto was placed under arrest, but pointed out that, in his official capacity, he could not state anything.

Since May 25, when it was announced by "The Shanghai Times" that charges would be framed against the two Italians the police would not reveal any details of the allegations. Detective Sub-Inspector Tilton had been working on the case together with the Italian authorities.

Bank Broken Into

It was reported that a total of $63,000 of cash and jewellery were stolen from the Pinto Bank between the closing time on Saturday, October 14, and 7.20 a.m. on Monday, October 16, when it was discovered by an office boy that the grille gates had been forced and the partition leading to the office of Mr. Pinto kicked in. Entrance to the bank was by a stairway leading to the offices over the establishment of Messrs. Chiyo Yoko. The thieves, upon getting into the office, drilled away the combination on the Chinese-made safe and gained access to some $50,000 in banknotes and $9,000 in diamond rings and other valuables.

Four Lawyers

It is understood that no fewer than four lawyers have been retained by Mr. Pinto and Mrs. Cacciopollì to appear in their defence. The four lawyers are Messrs. R. D'Auxion de Ruffe, G. Constantini, K. E. Newman and H. D. Rodger.

平托经讯问后
被逮捕

银行负责人持法院令状
被拘押于华德路监狱

明日将与一女子
一同受审

聘请四名律师辩护；领事馆内发生争执

意大利籍的平托银行（一家汇兑与贷款机构）经理兼董事V. 平托先生，上月月底收到传票，要求他于明日出席意大利领事法庭，就企图诈骗一家保险公司的指控进行答辩，此事曾由《字林西报》于5月25日独家报道。平托于周六晚被捕，昨日凭领事馆签发的令状被关押于华德路监狱，等候审判。

据悉，平托被捕是因为在领事当局与中央捕房侦探对先前指控进行调查期间，某些细节被揭露。

5月底，平托与A. 卡乔波利夫人（Mrs. A Caccioppoli）均收到传票，要求他们于6月9日（明日）上午出席意大利领事法庭，就企图诈骗一家保险公司的指控进行答辩。二人居住在兰心路216号，据悉在该处经营维克多酒店及意大利餐厅。该指控源于去年10月14日至16日那个周末发生在南京路166号一楼平托银行办事处的63,000美元现金及珠宝抢劫案，该案曾受到警方的彻底调查。据悉，相关保险公司拒绝支付保险金。曾向英国最高法院对该保险公司提起诉讼，但随后撤诉。

在向平托先生和卡乔波利夫人送达传票时，据信已有针对他们的有力证据，但后来又有更多事实被揭露，导致签发逮捕平托先生的令状。

据报道，中央捕房的侦探手持领事馆令状，于周六晚间前往兰心路的维克多酒店，在那里等候平托先生回家。他们将其逮捕并带回中央捕房，他在那里度过了一夜。

面见法官

上午，平托被带至意大利领事法庭，由领事法官R. 拉佩克斯骑士官长（Cav. Uff. R. Rapex）审问。据悉，在平托身处意大利领事法庭的短暂时间内，现场发生了几次争执，平托感到身体不适。最终，意大利当局发布命令，将平托关押于华德路监狱，等候明日上午与卡乔波利夫人一同出庭。

正如向这两名意大利人送达传票时一样，意大利当局和警方对针对平托和卡乔波利夫人的指控的确切性质保持完全沉默。拉佩克斯法官证实平托已被逮捕，但指出，以他的官方身份，他不能透露任何信息。

自5月25日《字林西报》宣布将对这两名意大利人提出指控以来，警方未透露任何指控细节。蒂尔顿副督察（Detective Sub-Inspector Tilton）一直与意大利当局共同处理此案。

银行遭闯入

据报道，在去年10月14日星期六关门时间至10月16日星期一上午7点20分之间，平托银行被盗走总计63,000美元的现金和珠宝。当时一名办公室勤杂工发现格栅门被撬开，通往平托先生办公室的隔板被踢破。进入银行的通道是一段楼梯，通向千代洋行（Messrs. Chiyo Yoko）店铺上方的办公室。窃贼进入办公室后，钻开了中国制造保险箱的密码锁，取走了约50,000美元纸币以及价值9,000美元的钻戒和其他贵重物品。

四名律师

据悉，平托先生和卡乔波利夫人已聘请了至少四名律师为其出庭辩护。这四名律师是R. 多克西翁·德·鲁夫（R. D'Auxion de Ruffe）、G. 康斯坦蒂尼（G. Constantini）、K. E. 纽曼（K. E. Newman）和H. D. 罗杰（H. D. Rodger）先生。

（右上角批注框内文字：上海公共租界工部局警务处 / S. 登记处 / B. D. 4777 / 日期 36年6月8日）

THE CHINA PRESS, TUESDAY, SEPTEMBER 17, 1935
11798
4777
17- 9- 35

Pinto Bank
Is Robbed
Of $63,000

Nanking Road Job Is
Daringly Executed
Over Week-End

SCREWDRIVER USED
TO GAIN ENTRANCE

Central Police Search
For Clues, Make
No Arrests

Central Police Station detectives were last night still searching for clues that might lead to the discovery of the identities of the persons who burgled the safe in the Pinto Bank, 80 Nanking Road, over the week-end and made good their escape with $63,000 in cash and jewelry.

Detectives in charge of the case last night told a CHINA PRESS reporter that while they were not altogether baffled, finding the culprits was likely to prove a difficult task. Some fingerprints are reported to have been found, but very little else that might be helpful to the police has been discovered.

Burglars broke into the Pinto Bank some time between 2 p.m. Saturday and 7.20 a.m. yesterday. The criminals effected an entrance through a stairway at 80 Nanking Road by the simple use of a screwdriver. They removed the screws fastening one side of the collapsible iron gate that closed the street entrance, pushed the gate aside and went in.

Access to the bank itself, after the gate had been opened, was comparatively easy. The institution is situated on the second floor of the building, and all that was necessary to effect an entrance was the breaking of the glass in the bank door.

The burglars, however, selected a more difficult method, that of removing a partition that separated the offices of the bank from the hallway.

Drilled Safe Open

Once inside the bank, the burglars made their way to the bank safe in Mr. V. Pinto's private office, drilled it open and took everything of value. They then broke open a drawer in Mr. Pinto's private desk but removed none of its contents.

The jewelry taken, mostly rings, was valued at $9,000 while the balance, about $54,000, was in currency. The loss was covered by insurance on a policy written by a local American company. The jewelry had been received by the bank as collateral on loans, but most of it had passed into the possession of the bank, it was stated.

Leaving the building, the burglars apparently retraced their steps and stopped long enough at the entrance to the stairway on Nanking Road to close the iron gate. They replaced one of the screws sufficient to hold the gate in place, giving the appearance to the ordinary passerby of not having been tampered with.

Police stated yesterday that opening the gate had proven quite a simple job, the screws used being only an inch long. Removing them, it was pointed out, had apparently been the work of only a few minutes.

How They Entered The Bank

All that was necessary when burglars sought to enter the Pinto Bank; 80 Nanking Road, was to remove the two screws fastening the handle to the iron gate that closed the street entrance. Above picture shows a workman, posing with the handle, just before he set about making necessary repairs.—CHINA PRESS Photo by A. Krause.

Bank Closed Saturday

Mr. Pinto stated yesterday that the bank had been closed shortly after 2 o'clock Saturday afternoon and the robbery was discovered by a Chinese employee who appeared on the premises at 7.20 o'clock yesterday morning. Examination of the safe revealed that it was of local make and proven fairly easy to drill through.

The bank is the sole property of Mr. Pinto, well-known Italian resident of Shanghai. It has been in operation since last November at the present location. It is a small institution dealing chiefly in exchange and small loans.

Burglary of the bank is the fourth spectacular raid by criminals in the downtown district of Shanghai during the past week. The first was the $91,000 Central Post Office robbery staged Monday morning, September 2. The second was the burglary of the Whiteaway, Laidlaw Department Store at the corner of Nanking and Szechuen Roads, perpetrated, it is believed by someone who had hidden inside the store when it was being locked up on the night of September 2. The third was a raid made by a band of armed robbers on the morning of September 3 on the National Construction Commission Purchasing Office, 34 Museum Road.

平托银行
被盗
63,000美元

南京路劫案于周末
大胆实施

使用螺丝刀
进入

中央捕房搜寻线索，
未实施逮捕

中央捕房的侦探昨晚仍在搜寻线索，以期查明上周末闯入南京路80号平托银行保险箱并携63,000美元现金和珠宝逃脱者的身份。

负责此案的侦探昨晚告诉《大美晚报》记者，虽然他们并未完全束手无策，但查明罪犯可能是一项艰巨的任务。据报道发现了一些指纹，但几乎没有其他对警方有帮助的发现。

窃贼是在上周六下午2点至昨天上午7点20分之间的某个时间闯入平托银行的。罪犯仅用一把螺丝刀，便通过南京路80号的楼梯入口进入。他们卸下了固定关闭街道入口的折叠铁门一侧的螺丝，将门推到一边后进入。

打开铁门后，进入银行本身相对容易。该机构位于大楼二楼，要进入只需打破银行门上的玻璃。

然而，窃贼选择了一种更困难的方法，即拆除将银行办公室与走廊隔开的隔板。

钻开保险箱

进入银行后，窃贼来到V. 平托先生私人办公室内的银行保险箱处，将其钻开并拿走了所有贵重物品。随后他们撬开了平托先生私人办公桌的一个抽屉，但未拿走其中的任何物品。

被盗珠宝主要为戒指，价值9,000美元，其余约54,000美元为现钞。损失由一家本地美国公司承保的保单覆盖。据悉，这些珠宝是银行作为贷款抵押品接收的，但大部分已归银行所有。

离开大楼时，窃贼显然原路返回，并在南京路楼梯入口处停留了足够长的时间以关闭铁门。他们重新拧上了一颗足以固定铁门的螺丝，使普通路人看来铁门未被触动。

警方昨日表示，打开铁门证明是一项相当简单的工作，所使用的螺丝仅有一英寸长。指出卸下这些螺丝显然只需几分钟。

他们如何进入银行

窃贼试图进入南京路80号平托银行时，只需卸下两颗将把手固定在关闭街道入口的铁门上的螺丝。上图显示一名工人在着手进行必要维修之前，手持把手摆姿势拍照。——《大美晚报》照片，A. Krause摄。

银行周六关闭

平托先生昨日表示，银行于上周六下午2点后不久关闭，抢劫案是由一名于昨天早上7点20分到达现场的中国雇员发现的。对保险箱的检查显示，其为本地制造，事实证明很容易钻透。

该银行为上海知名意大利居民平托先生的独资财产。自去年11月以来，该银行一直在现址运营。这是一家小型机构，主要经营汇兑和小额贷款业务。

此次银行盗窃案是过去一周上海市中心地区发生的第四起引人注目的罪犯突袭事件。第一起是9月2日星期一上午发生的91,000美元中央邮局抢劫案。第二起是南京路与四川路路口惠罗公司（Whiteaway, Laidlaw Department Store）百货商店的盗窃案，据信是有人在9月2日晚商店锁门时藏匿店内所为。第三起是9月3日上午，一伙武装劫匪对博物馆路34号全国建设委员会采购办公室进行的突袭。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY. AUGUST 17, 1935.
H777
17-8-35

Commotion On Nanking Rd.
Caused By Robber Alarm

Police Rush To Pinto Bank, Find Only A Quarrel
Between Bank Proprietor And Customer; No.
Charge Laid Although Pistol Involved

Intense excitement, hubbub and alarm was occasioned yesterday afternoon in the vicinity of 60 Nanking Road as a Police van, rushed in a hurry from Central Station, drew up outside the premises of the Pinto Bank. Police officers, answering an alarm of armed robbery, rushed upstairs to the Bank offices, to discover that all that was happening was a quarrel between Mr. Vincent Pinto, proprietor of the Bank, and a Chinese customer armed with a pistol, which he was alleged to have used in a threatening manner.

Mr. Pinto and his manager, and the Chinese customer, were all escorted to Central Station, where detectives spent the best part of two hours trying to make a coherent story out of several depositions. When the inquiry was over, the trio departed with much noise and gesticulation and the Police announced that no charge would be laid.

It was ascertained that the Chinese customer who was alleged to have threatened Mr. Pinto with his pistol, was a well-known member of the Gold Bar Exchange. His pistol, which he carries as a means of protection in view of the large sums of money which he frequently has about his person, was found to be licensed both for the Settlement and the French Concession.

Exactly what the quarrel was about was not disclosed. At all events, there were no witnesses to testify that the Chinese customer had drawn his pistol. The alarm which brought the Police to the scene was raised by Mr. Pinto's excitable lady secretary, who yelled at the top of her voice when the quarrel had assumed what appeared to her to be menacing proportions.

南京路骚动
由抢劫警报引起

警察冲向平托银行，发现仅是
银行主与顾客间的争吵；虽涉手枪，
但未提出指控

昨日下午，南京路60号附近发生了剧烈的兴奋、喧哗和恐慌，一辆从中央捕房匆忙赶来的警车停在了平托银行 premises 外。警官们响应武装抢劫的警报，冲上楼进入银行办公室，却发现正在发生的只是银行主人文森特·平托先生与一名中国顾客之间的争吵，该顾客持有一把手枪，据称他以威胁的方式使用了该手枪。

平托先生及其经理，以及该名中国顾客，均被护送至中央捕房，侦探们花了近两个小时的时间，试图从几份证词中梳理出一个连贯的故事。询问结束后，这三人大声喧哗、手舞足蹈地离开，警方宣布不提出任何指控。

经查实，据称用手枪威胁平托先生的这名中国顾客是金业交易所（Gold Bar Exchange）的知名成员。鉴于他随身携带大量现金，他将手枪作为保护手段携带，经查该手枪在公共租界和法租界均持有执照。

争吵的具体原因未予披露。无论如何，没有证人作证说这名中国顾客拔出了手枪。引来警察的警报是由平托先生易激动的女秘书发出的，当争吵在她看来呈现出威胁性的规模时，她大声尖叫。
